claim: A Politburo press conference on 9 November 1989 prematurely announced that East Germans could travel without restrictions.
excerpt: occurred after a Politburo press conference on 9 November 1989 prematurely announced that East Germans could travel without restrictions

claim: The press conference was led by Günter Schabowski, began at 18:00 CET on 9 November, and was broadcast live on East German television and radio.
excerpt: led by Günter Schabowski, the outgoing party leader in East Berlin and top party spokesman as Secretary for Information, beginning at 18:00 CET on 9 November and broadcast live on East German television and radio

claim: Shortly before the press conference Schabowski was handed a note announcing the changes, but given no further instructions on how to handle the information.
excerpt: Shortly before the press conference, he was handed a note from Krenz announcing the changes, but given no further instructions on how to handle the information.
context: He had not been involved in the discussions about the new regulations and had not been fully updated.

claim: Asked when the regulations would take effect, Schabowski replied that, as far as he knew, it takes effect immediately, without delay.
excerpt: Schabowski replied, "As far as I know, it takes effect immediately, without delay"
context: Wikipedia gives this as an English rendering of the German; it calls his answer an apparent assumption based on the note's opening paragraph.

claim: West German news told viewers that East Germany's borders were open: the dpa bulletin at 19:04 said citizens could cross the inner German border "immediately", and ARD's Tagesthemen said the borders were open to everyone.
excerpt: The West German Deutsche Presse-Agentur issued a bulletin at 19:04 which reported that East German citizens would be able to cross the inner German border "immediately".
context: Tagesthemen anchor Hanns Joachim Friedrichs: the GDR announced that, starting immediately, its borders are open to everyone.

claim: At 22:45 (alternatively given as 23:30) on 9 November, Harald Jäger, commander of the Bornholmer Straße crossing, yielded and let guards open the checkpoints.
excerpt: at 22:45 (alternatively given as 23:30) on 9 November, Harald Jäger, commander of the Bornholmer Straße border crossing, yielded, allowing guards to open the checkpoints
